subject: CrossoverTech replacement: performance escrow & equitable reprice
messages:
From: Alex Garrison <alex.garrison@crossovertech.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: procure@crossovertech.com
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Vendor swap — questions on pricing & performance escrow

Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo last week. The engineering team ran a short benchmark with Redwood in our staging environment and the numbers look promising. Procurement has pushed back on economics and wants to understand two things before we move to a pilot:

1) Can Redwood match the incumbent's blended cost after committed usage? They quoted us a blended $0.0018/token equivalent for our mix.
2) We want a lightweight "performance escrow" — a measurable SLA exhibit that ties latency breaches to unit credits for the pilot and first 3 months after go-live.

Can you provide a concrete counteroffer and an SLA exhibit we can share with our legal team? If this lines up, we can fast-track a PO.

Appreciate a clear table of what you can commit to (pricing by tier, credits for latency >95th pctl, and any one-time onboarding credits).

Best,
Alex
Head of Platform, CrossoverTech

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
To: Alex Garrison <alex.garrison@crossovertech.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-30T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor swap — questions on pricing & performance escrow

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and for running the staging checks. Great to hear the baseline numbers looked good.

Quick summary of what I can commit to now (we'll route final language to legal/finance):
- Pricing: For pilot (3 months) we can match incumbent blended at $0.0018/token equivalent for up to 120M tokens total. After pilot, tiered list pricing with a 12-month committed consumption schedule: first 6 months at $0.0021, months 7–12 at $0.00195, volume-based true-up quarterly.
- Onboarding credit: one-time $25k credit to offset migration/engineering work.
- Performance escrow / SLA exhibit: we propose a simple exhibit: if 95th-percentile latency for the production route exceeds 400ms for >3 days in a rolling 7-day window, CrossoverTech receives a credit equal to 5% of that month's consumption up to a cap of $15k. The full exhibit (technical metrics, measurement windows, and adjudication steps) attached.

Attaching the proposal PDF and a CSV with the latency thresholds and examples. If that looks directionally right I can pull Marissa in to confirm the commercial cadence and Priya to scope the pilot success criteria & runbook.

Next steps I suggest:
- Quick 30-min call Tues/Wed to agree on thresholds + credit cap
- If agreed, Redwood issues an updated SOW and DocuSign link for the pilot PO

Can you confirm availability for a short sync?

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-proposal-v2.pdf (proposal, 6 pages)
Attachment: latency-sla-exhibit.csv (CSV, thresholds + sample calc)
From: Alex Garrison <alex.garrison@crossovertech.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: procure@crossovertech.com
Date: 2026-08-31T08:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor swap — questions on pricing & performance escrow

Rafael — this is helpful, thanks. A couple of clarifying items from procurement & infra: 

- Procurement wants the pilot pricing to be guaranteed for the pilot period (i.e., no retroactive true-ups during the 3 months). Is that acceptable?
- For the SLA credit: legal asked whether credits are automatic based on your telemetry or require a dispute process. They prefer an automatic calculation with option to dispute within 10 business days.
- Regarding the $25k credit, would Redwood consider a split credit structure: $15k applied immediately to the pilot invoice, $10k applied as migration hours to be used within 90 days? That helps our invoice planning.

We can take a 30-min call tomorrow at 10:00am PT if that works for you.

Alex

---
On Aug 30, 2026, at 11:05 AM, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai wrote:
> Alex — thanks for the clear ask and for running the staging checks. Great to hear the baseline numbers looked good.
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-31T12:10:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Vendor swap — questions on pricing & performance escrow

Looping finance and product so we have internal alignment before the sync. Rafael — notes below and a suggested slight tweak to limit downstream exposure: 

1) Pilot pricing guarantee: we can guarantee the pilot fixed rate for the pilot invoice cycle (no true-ups) up to the committed 120M token cap. Any overage will be billed at the agreed post-pilot tier.
2) SLA credit automation: we can automate measurement and credit calculation from our telemetry, but advise a short dispute window (10 business days) with a formal review path — keeps it operationally clean.
3) Credit structure: prefer the $25k credit applied $15k to pilot invoice, $10k as engineering hours credit — but logistically we need the hours to be consumed within 60 days to avoid open liability. Priya: can your team commit to a 60-day window?

If everyone is aligned, finance will draft the commercial term language (simple exhibit) and legal will tie the dispute steps into the SOW. Rafael — please push the 10:00am PT call on the calendar and include the proposed exhibit as an agenda item.

-Marissa
VP, Commercial Operations — Redwood Inference

From: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-31T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Vendor swap — questions on pricing & performance escrow

Marissa — 60-day window for engineering-hours credit is doable if we scope the migration tasks up front. I'll draft a pilot success checklist that maps to observable metrics (95th pctl latency, request error rate, KV cache hit ratio, and model continuity checks). Rafael — I'll bring the checklist to the sync and propose specific telemetry endpoints we should publish to Crossover for transparency.

Also flag: if they want auto credits, we need to lock down measurement sources (our edge telemetry + their synthetic canary). Recommend a dual-measure approach: Redwood telemetry triggers the credit calculation, and Crossover's canary data can be submitted as part of disputes. This avoids noisy one-sided adjudication.

Priya Natarajan
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
To: Alex Garrison <alex.garrison@crossovertech.com>, procure@crossovertech.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priya_natarajan@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-02T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor swap — questions on pricing & performance escrow

Alex — appreciate the quick turn. Confirming the call tomorrow at 10:00am PT (calendar invite sent).

To summarize what's on the agenda and what we'll bring: 
- Pilot invoice guarantee: fixed rate for pilot at $0.0018/token up to 120M tokens (no retroactive pilot true-ups) — Marissa will confirm term language.
- Credit structure: $25k total (split $15k immediate pilot invoice credit, $10k engineering-hours credit to be used within 60 days).
- SLA exhibit: automated credit calc from Redwood telemetry, 10-business-day dispute window; draft exhibit attached.
- Priya will run through the pilot success checklist + telemetry endpoints.

Attachments: redwood-proposal-v2.pdf, latency-sla-exhibit.csv

If anything else you'd like covered, drop it here and we'll add it to the agenda. Looking forward to closing this pilot fast.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
